comment: Review scoring under the Martian Code Review Bench and CR-Bench protocols, over a diff with three planted
defects. **The corpus is small and reproducible offline**; the protocols are the field standard, the corpus is not.
**This is not a Martian-comparable figure and must not be quoted as one.** A score from a different corpus
is not a comparison. What it is: a protocol-faithful number on a corpus we control, which is what an
**SNR is reported because precision alone hides over-generation**, which the field numbers show -
single-pass GPT-5.2 reaches 27.0% recall at 3.6% precision.

protocol.review: Martian Code Review Bench shape: per-diff precision / recall / F1
protocol.signalToNoise: CR-Bench: true positives over all comments emitted

reasons: the quoted code does not appear at lines 8-8
andTheGatesEffect.note: **The prediction was written down before this ran**: QASecClaw (arXiv 2605.01885) takes a scanner from F1 78.39% to 90.93% by cutting false positives 88.6% at a 3.1% recall cost, so precision should rise more than recall falls. **This figure is the test of that**, and it is recorded whether or not it agrees.

andTheFieldForScale.note: Quoted with their dates and arms, as the competitive analysis insists; none of them is this corpus.

andWhatThisCannotSay: **Nothing about Martian.** Its corpus is ~300,000 real PRs, continuously sampled to resist memorisation; ours is one diff written for this file.
**Nothing about generalisation.** Three planted defects in one language say nothing about the long tail.
**Nothing about the arms.** Martian runs two arms designed to disagree, and which one is reported changes the number.
